summary: Wide main menu and loading screen from the new art (full in wide, centre crop in letterbox)
author: pm
body:
Rebuild the main menu from the user's wide art. Source sheet: working/classic_ui/hd/main_menu.png (1920x1300, the user's; read-only, also main_menu.psd / main_menu_no_text.png). It holds:
- the 1920x1080 background at (0,0), with logo and title baked in;
- a hover plate, 296x39, translucent white (alpha about 51), at (16,1100);
- labels for Log In (x 337-447), New Account (476-721) and Exit (750-821), as black at y 1108 and gold at y 1148, each 24 px tall.

User, 2026-11-25: picked layout A ("A, under the title"). Mockup: .claude/scratch/coordinator/main_menu_wide/menu_a.png, script compose.py beside it.

Layout A, in 1920x1080 art pixels:
- buttons stacked and centred on x 1408 (the centre of "THE HELDENIAN PROJECT"), at y 360, 416 and 472 (56 px apart);
- normal item: the black label as a 2 px drop shadow, then the label in bone (226, 214, 192);
- hover: the plate centred behind the label, then the shadow, then the gold label.

These are guesses the user may correct: black as the shadow, the plate as the hover highlight, and the bone colour for the normal state (not in the sheet).

Today: screen_main_menu.cpp draws InterfaceNdMainMenu frame 0 at (0,0) in the 640x480 view and puts three cc::button controls at x 465 (y 238/276/315, 164x22), as of 2026-11-25.

Open questions for the plan:
- how a 16:9 backdrop should fit 4:3, letterbox and stretch outputs (Helbreath-SDL uses a centre-cropped cover fit for front-end backdrops);
- where the button hit areas sit at each aspect;
- how the art gets into staged/ (a sprite folder vs a single image) and at what resolution;
- whether the version text and copyright lines stay.

**Done when:** the main menu shows the wide art with layout A at 16:9 and a sensible crop at 4:3; hover, click and keyboard focus work through CControls; both builds are clean; screenshots at 4:3 and 16:9 are attached.

Source: user in chat, 2026-11-25.

**Scope update, 2026-11-25 (user):**
- "These are some widescreen additions - if the resolution is in wide screen we should offer the full view. If we are in letterbox we should chop off the sides and only present the center"
- "These should replace the existing"

Assets, all in working/classic_ui/hd (the user's folder; read-only, copy into staged/):
- main_menu_no_text.png (1920x1300): replaces the main menu backdrop, intermediate_screens sprite 1 frame 0 (800x600).
- loading_screen.png (1924x1128): the 1920x1080-ish backdrop plus "Loading Data ..." labels in white and gold below it. Replaces the loading screen sprite (screen_loading.cpp:38).
- interface.pak-001_x4.png goes to HH-0083 (the label sheet).

Rules:
- Wide output (stretch / widescreen) shows the full 16:9 image.
- Letterbox shows the centre 4:3 crop (1440x1080 of 1920x1080).
- Layout A's buttons at art x 1408 +-148 stay inside the crop (x 240-1680), measured.

Researcher findings, 2026-11-25 (read-only, Sonnet):
- The logical UI is 800x600, not 640x480 (resolution_config.h:14).
- No call exposes the visible window extent in UI units. Add IRenderer::get_screen_extent() from current_screen_mapping().view (sfml_renderer.cpp:391).
- Draw the backdrop with create_texture_from_file(smooth) and draw_texture_region (the minimap and kits use the same path).
- Re-lay-out the cc::buttons each frame with set_local_bounds; mouse mapping already allows out-of-range UI units in stretch (sfml_window.cpp:860).

**Correction, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'The buttons should always have a background and the font should move to gold when hovered - otherwise remaining black'. Every button always has the plate behind it; the label is black normally and gold when hovered or focused. There is no bone tint and no shadow. This replaces the layout A styling above. Sent to the working agent.

**Change, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'For the button backgrounds, can we increase the size by 1.5x same with the font. Then use additive blending for the button background'. The plate and labels are drawn at 1.5x; the plate uses additive blending; spacing scales to about 84 art px (y 360/444/528) so the plates do not overlap. Sent to the working agent.

**Clarified, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'I just want to see it not set it in stone', then '1.5x is set in stone just not the additive'. The 1.5x plate and labels are final; the plate stays normal alpha. Additive is a preview only, mocked up for the user.

**Decided, 2026-11-25 (user):** after a preview of additive plates at 20%, 35% and 50% (.claude/scratch/coordinator/main_menu_wide/menu_15x_additive_opacity.png): 'If that is the case, I like the additive look so we can keep it'. The plate is additive at 50% opacity (one named constant, tunable). Sent to the working agent.

**Revised, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'I think we'll stick with the 20% as we had'. The plate stays additive at the sheet's own alpha (about 20%), not 50%. Sent to the working agent.

**Change, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'The loading screen text should also be drawn with our ttf for Times New Roman if possible'. The 'Loading Data ...' text is drawn live in Liberation Serif (the Times New Roman metric clone, already shipped), matching the art's size and white/gold colours, instead of the baked labels. Sent to the working agent.

**Clarified, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'Basically the client would need to pre-render the font, then draw it and do exactly what we are doing with the sprite text'. At screen init, 'Loading Data ...' is rendered from Liberation Serif into high-resolution white and gold textures at art resolution. They are then drawn exactly like the menu's sheet labels (art-pixel placement, smooth scale, the same cover mapping). There is no per-frame TTF layout.

**Asset, 2026-11-25 (user):** working/classic_ui/hd/loading_screen_no_text.png (1920x1080, measured) is the loading backdrop; it replaces loading_screen.png as the source. Sent to the working agent.

**Change, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'the main menu buttons can be shrunk by 25% and moved to match the original positions better'. Scale 1.125x (1.5 x 0.75). Centres are the old 800x600 button centres mapped through the art's 4:3 centre region (scale 1.8, x offset 240): x 1225, y 448/517/586. Mockup: .claude/scratch/coordinator/main_menu_wide/menu_1125x_additive.png. Sent to the working agent.

**Change, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'Bump it up 15%', read as size: the plate and labels are now 1.29375x (1.125 x 1.15); centres unchanged. Mockup: menu_129x_additive.png. Sent to the working agent.

**Approved, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'Better - and make sure they are positioned relative to the original'. Size 1.29375x is final. Button centres are derived in code from the original 800x600 rects through one named mapping (art_x = 240 + x * 1.8, art_y = y * 1.8), then through the backdrop's cover transform; no hard-coded art coordinates. Sent to the working agent.

**Final, 2026-11-25 (user):** 'Round up to 1.3'. The button plate and labels are drawn at 1.3x.

**Verified, 2026-11-25:** review PASS (two rounds), Windows Debug and Linux client builds clean, deployed. In-client checks at 4:3 (1280x960) and 16:9 (1600x900 window): menu hover, focus and every button; HUD digits and magic numerals at 1280x960. Ultra-wide loading label checked by the math only (top 534-536 at 21:9 and 2.4:1). Untested: real fullscreen on a 16:9 display, ultra-wide in the client, the magic shop, running on Linux.
